verses.1:1: Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: I give thanks to my God upon every remembrance of you,
verses.1:4: always in every petition of mine on behalf of all of you, making this petition with joy,
verses.1:5: because of your participation in the gospel from the first day until now,
verses.1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who began a good work in you will carry it to completion until the day of Christ Jesus;
verses.1:7: just as it is right for me to think this way concerning all of you, because I hold you in my heart, since both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, all of you are fellow partners with me of grace.
verses.1:8: For God is my witness how I long for all of you with the deep affection of Christ Jesus.
verses.1:9: And this I pray, that your love may abound still more and more in full knowledge and all discernment,
verses.1:10: so that you may approve the things that excel, in order that you may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,
verses.1:11: having been filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
verses.1:12: Now I want you to know, brothers, that the things concerning me have turned out rather for the advancement of the gospel,
verses.1:13: so that my chains have become clearly known in Christ throughout the entire praetorian guard and to all the rest,
verses.1:14: and most of the brothers, having gained confidence in the Lord through my chains, are far more daring to speak the word of God without fear.
verses.1:15: Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and strife, yet others also out of goodwill.
verses.1:16: The latter do so out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel;
verses.1:17: but the former proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, supposing to stir up affliction in my chains.
verses.1:18: What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will rejoice,
verses.1:19: for I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your petition and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
verses.1:20: according to my eager expectation and hope that I will be put to shame in nothing, but that with all boldness, as always, so also now Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
verses.1:21: For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
verses.1:22: But if living in the flesh means fruit of labor for me—then what I will choose, I cannot tell.
verses.1:23: Yet I am hard-pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, for that is very much better;
verses.1:24: but to remain on in the flesh is more necessary on your account.
verses.1:25: And being confident of this, I know that I will remain and continue alongside all of you for your advancement and joy of faith,
verses.1:26: so that your ground for boasting in Christ Jesus may abound on my account through my coming to you again.
verses.1:27: Only conduct yourselves as citizens worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear about you that you are standing firm in one spirit, with one soul striving side by side for the faith of the gospel,
verses.1:28: and in nothing terrified by those who oppose you (which is to them a proof of destruction, yet of your salvation, and this from God,
verses.1:29: because it has been graciously granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer on His behalf),
verses.1:30: having the same struggle that you saw in me and now hear to be in me.
verses.2:1: Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender affection and compassion,
verses.2:2: make my joy complete, that you be of the same mind, having the same love, united in soul, thinking the one thing,
verses.2:3: doing nothing from selfish ambition or vain conceit, but with humility of mind considering one another as surpassing yourselves,
verses.2:4: not each looking out for his own interests, but each also for the interests of others.
verses.2:5: Hold this mindset among yourselves, which was also in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:6: who, existing in the form of God, did not consider being equal with God a thing to be seized,
verses.2:7: but emptied Himself by taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of human beings; and being found in outward appearance as a man,
verses.2:8: He humbled Himself, becoming obedient up to death—indeed, death on a cross.
verses.2:9: For this reason God also supremely exalted Him and graciously granted Him the name that is above every name,
verses.2:10: so that at the name of Jesus every knee may bow, of those in heaven and on earth and beneath the earth,
verses.2:11: and every tongue may openly confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
verses.2:12: Consequently, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed—not only as in my presence, but now far more in my absence—work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
verses.2:13: for God is the One working in you both to will and to work for the sake of His good pleasure.
verses.2:14: Do everything without grumbling and disputes,
verses.2:15: so that you may become blameless and pure, unblemished children of God in the midst of a crooked and twisted generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,
verses.2:16: holding fast to the word of life, for a ground of boasting for me on the day of Christ, that I did not run in vain nor labor in vain.
verses.2:17: Yet even if I am being poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice together with all of you.
verses.2:18: And in the same way, you also rejoice and rejoice together with me.
verses.2:19: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I also may be cheered when I learn about your circumstances.
verses.2:20: For I have no one of kindred soul who will genuinely care for the things concerning you,
verses.2:21: for they all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
verses.2:22: But you know his proven worth, that as a child with a father, he served with me for the gospel.
verses.2:23: Therefore I hope to send him at once, as soon as I see how things turn out for me;
verses.2:24: and I am confident in the Lord that I myself will also come soon.
verses.2:25: Yet I considered it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier, and your messenger and minister to my need,
verses.2:26: since he was longing for all of you and was deeply distressed because you had heard that he was ill.
verses.2:27: For indeed he was ill, coming close to death; but God had mercy on him, and not on him only, but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.
verses.2:28: Therefore I have sent him all the more eagerly, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less sorrowful.
verses.2:29: Receive him then in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
verses.2:30: because for the work of Christ he came close to death, risking his life to supply what was lacking in your service toward me.
verses.3:1: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. Writing the same things to you is not tiresome for me, and for you it is a safeguard.
verses.3:2: Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the mutilation.
verses.3:3: For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and place no confidence in the flesh,
verses.3:4: although I myself also have confidence in the flesh. If any other person thinks he may place confidence in the flesh, I even more:
verses.3:5: circumcised on the eighth day, from the lineage of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; with respect to the law, a Pharisee;
verses.3:6: with respect to zeal, persecuting the church; with respect to the righteousness that is in the law, having become blameless.
verses.3:7: But whatever things were gains to me, these I have counted as loss because of Christ.
verses.3:8: Even more than that, I also count all things to be loss because of the surpassing excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, on account of whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and I count them as refuse so that I may gain Christ
verses.3:9: and be found in Him, not having a righteousness of my own from the law, but the one through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God based on faith,
verses.3:10: in order to know Him and the power of His resurrection and fellowship in His sufferings, being conformed to His death,
verses.3:11: if somehow I may arrive at the resurrection from the dead.
verses.3:12: Not that I have already obtained it or have already been perfected, but I pursue it, if indeed I may take hold of that for which I was also taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
verses.3:13: Brothers, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of it; yet one thing I do: forgetting the things behind and stretching forward to the things ahead,
verses.3:14: I pursue toward the goal for the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:15: Therefore, as many of us as are mature, let us think this way; and if in anything you think differently, God will reveal this to you as well.
verses.3:16: Only, to the point we have attained, let us keep in step along that same line.
verses.3:17: Become fellow imitators of me, brothers, and observe closely those who walk in this way, just as you have us as a pattern.
verses.3:18: For many walk, about whom I often told you and now also say while weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ,
verses.3:19: whose end is destruction, whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who have their minds set on earthly things.
verses.3:20: For our citizenship is in the heavens, from where we also eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.3:21: who will transform the body of our lowliness to be conformed to the body of His glory, according to the working by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself.
verses.4:1: So then, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joy and crown, stand firm in this way in the Lord, beloved.
verses.4:2: I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.
verses.4:3: Yes, I also ask you, genuine companion, assist these women, who contended alongside me in the gospel along with Clement as well and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
verses.4:4: Rejoice in the Lord always; I will say again, rejoice.
verses.4:5: Let your gentleness be known to all people. The Lord is near.
verses.4:6: Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, through prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
verses.4:7: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will stand guard over your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:8: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are noble, whatever things are righteous, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are admirable, if there is any excellence and if there is any praise, consider these things.
verses.4:9: The things that you learned and received and heard and saw in me, put these into practice, and the God of peace will be with you.
verses.4:10: Now I rejoiced greatly in the Lord because now at last you have made your concern for me flourish again; indeed, you were concerned about this, yet you had no opportunity.
verses.4:11: Not that I speak out of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am to be content.
verses.4:12: I know how to be brought low, and I also know how to abound; in every situation and in all things I have learned the secret, both to be well fed and to go hungry, both to abound and to suffer lack.
verses.4:13: I have strength for all things in the One who empowers me.
verses.4:14: Nevertheless, you did well by sharing with me in my affliction.
verses.4:15: And you yourselves also know, Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me in the account of giving and receiving except you alone,
verses.4:16: for even in Thessalonica you sent to me both once and twice for my need.
verses.4:17: Not that I am seeking the gift, but I am seeking the fruit that increases to your account.
verses.4:18: Now I have received everything in full and I abound; I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you, a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
verses.4:19: And my God will fill every need of yours according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:20: And to our God and Father be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:21: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers with me greet you.
verses.4:22: All the saints greet you, and especially those from Caesar's household.
verses.4:23: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen!

notes.1:7: The Greek infinitive phrase is grammatically ambiguous and can be read either as "because I hold you in my heart" or "because you hold me in your heart," though the former best fits the immediate context.
notes.1:13: Greek "praitorion" can refer either to the imperial (praetorian) guard in Rome or to a Roman governor's official headquarters/palace in a province.
notes.1:19: Echoing Job 13:16 (LXX), Greek "soteria" ("salvation") may encompass both Paul's deliverance or vindication before the court and his ultimate salvation before God.
notes.1:27: The verb "politeuesthe" means "conduct yourselves as citizens," a pointed civic metaphor for believers residing in the Roman colony of Philippi.
notes.2:5: Because the relative clause omits a verb in Greek, it may point either to Christ's own example ("which was also in Christ Jesus") or to the mindset believers share in union with Him ("which is also yours in Christ Jesus").
notes.2:6: The rare Greek noun "harpagmos" ("a thing to be seized") is much debated; it can denote either something not yet possessed to be grasped at or an existing privilege not to be exploited for selfish advantage.
notes.2:15: The Greek verb "phainesthe" has the same form in the indicative and imperative, so it can be read either as a statement ("you shine") or as a command ("shine").
notes.2:16: The Greek participle "epechontes" can mean either "holding fast to" (retaining) or "holding forth" (offering to the world) the word of life.
notes.3:2: Greek katatome ("mutilation," literally "a cutting down") forms a sharp wordplay with peritome ("circumcision") in v. 3.
notes.3:8: Greek skybala ("refuse") is a strong term for discarded waste, scraps, or excrement, emphasizing the stark contrast with knowing Christ.
notes.3:9: The Greek phrase pisteos Christou is debated and may be rendered either as an objective genitive ("faith in Christ") or a subjective genitive ("the faithfulness of Christ").
notes.3:20: Greek politeuma ("citizenship") can also denote a "commonwealth" or "colony," language with particular resonance for believers living in the Roman colony of Philippi.
notes.4:3: Greek gnesie syzyge ("genuine companion," literally "true yokefellow") may address an unnamed coworker or treat Syzygos as a personal name ("Syzygus").
notes.4:5: Greek to epieikes ("gentleness") conveys gracious forbearance or reasonableness; "The Lord is near" may refer either to Christ's imminent return or to His continual presence.
notes.4:12: Greek memyemai ("I have learned the secret") literally means "I have been initiated," drawing on terminology associated with ancient mystery cults.
notes.4:13: The critical Greek text reads simply "in the One who empowers me," without the explicit name "Christ" added in later manuscripts.
notes.4:23: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes the closing "Amen!" attested in many manuscripts, though some early witnesses omit it.
